title: All People That on Earth Do Dwell
description: All People That on Earth Do Dwell (Psalm 100) in Tonic Solfa, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, all five verses and a piano.
about: William Kethe's paraphrase of Psalm 100 was printed in the Anglo-Genevan psalter of 1561, and it has been sung to this tune ever since — the reason the melody is called OLD HUNDREDTH. It is the same tune as the Doxology, so a choir that can sing one can sing the other.
underlay: All peo-ple that on earth do dwell, Sing to the Lord with cheer-ful voice; Him serve with mirth, his praise forth tell, Come ye be-fore him and re-joice.

lines: All people that on earth do dwell,
Sing to the Lord with cheerful voice;
Him serve with mirth, his praise forth tell,
Come ye before him and rejoice.
The Lord, ye know, is God indeed;
Without our aid he did us make;
We are his folk, he doth us feed,
And for his sheep he doth us take.
O enter then his gates with praise,
Approach with joy his courts unto;
Praise, laud, and bless his name always,
For it is seemly so to do.
For why? the Lord our God is good;
His mercy is for ever sure;
His truth at all times firmly stood,
And shall from age to age endure.

verses.label: Doxology
verses.note: A closing doxology added in later psalters.
lines: To Father, Son and Holy Ghost,
The God whom heaven and earth adore,
From men and from the angel host
Be praise and glory evermore.
